text:
alex: Quick summary from today's quant sweep on atlas10b: INT4 gives ~2.6x token-cost reduction vs INT8 and ~4.3x vs fp16 on long-context generation, but shows a consistent 33% regression on multi-turn factuality-sensitive slices.

priya: Can you post a failing example + traffic profile?

alex: Example (sanitized):
```
PROMPT: answer multi-turn Q/A using meeting context (~3500 tokens)
FP16: correctly attributes figure to Q3 revenue
INT4: attributes figure to Q2 (hallucinated)
```
Traffic: slice=multi-turn-factuality, avg_tokens_in=3500, canary=5%. Cost per request: fp16 $0.024, INT8 $0.011, INT4 $0.0042.

eval-bot: Automated alert: multi-turn-factuality fail rate moved 2.8% -> 6.4% on atlas10b.int4 (threshold 3%).

sam: Looks like KV precision loss + longer KV chains for multi-turn. For product: recommend default INT4 for single-turn workloads (chat summaries, short answers) and INT8 for multi-turn or high-stakes flows.

priya: For GTN blurb: "Recommendation: Use INT4 as default for low-risk, single-turn endpoints to capture ~60-70% cost savings; route multi-turn/high-recall endpoints to INT8 to avoid a measurable factuality regression. Offer INT4 as opt-in for long-form customers with clear visibility (entity_f1, factuality_fail_rate dashboards) and an SLA carveout."

alex: Ops rollout plan: 1) implement route_by_feature (feature=turns OR tokens_in>2500) with fallback; 2) run 24h A/B smoke comparing INT4 vs INT8 on target slices; 3) monitor factuality_fail_rate, KV-hit-stability, p95 latency; 4) rollback if factuality_fail_rate > 3% AND delta>1.5% over 30m.

tess: Also note: disabling prefix caching for INT4 reduced regression by ~0.8pt in staging; include that as interim mitigation.

priya: I'll draft the one-paragraph GTN guidance with unit econ numbers and UX caveats. alex, attach failing examples + the routing PR.

alex: Will do. eval-bot: schedule 24h A/B smoke on multi-turn-factuality slice.

eval-bot: Scheduled.
